1.

The applicant has approached this Court under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seeking pre-arrest bail.

The apprehension of arrest is in connection with Crime Register No.
289 of 2023 registered with Taloja Police Station.

The offences alleged are under Sections 328, 467,
468, 471, 292, 273, 188 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 26(2)(i),
26, 27, and 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text: The prosecution case, in short, is that on 28 October 2022, at about 5:30 a.m., PI Shinge and Kamble noticed a Ballero tempo bearing registration No. MH-04/JK-8429 coming from Mumbra side.
The police party stopped the tempo near the toll plaza and 6-aba-2861-2023.doc carried out inspection.
On checking, it was found to be carrying tobacco, pan masala, gutkha, and other such articles, collectively valued at Rs.10,15,780/-.
The persons apprehended from the tempo disclosed that the said contraband was purchased from the present applicant.
On this basis, the FIR came to be registered.
3. The learned Advocate appearing for the applicant submitted that this Court, by order dated 12 October 2023, granted interim protection to the applicant.
The applicant has not misused the liberty so granted and has cooperated in the investigation.
The investigation is now complete and charge-sheet has been filed.
Hence, it is prayed that the interim order of protection be made absolute.
4. On the other hand, the learned APP opposed the application.
It was contended that the allegations against the applicant are serious in nature.
Considering the gravity of the offence, the application ought to be rejected.

It was further submitted that after the passing of the interim order,
an additional charge under Section 467 of the Indian Penal Code has also been added by the prosecution.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the material placed on record.
It is not in dispute that the applicant was granted interim protection by order dated 12 October 2023.
From the record, it is clear that during this period the applicant has not misused the liberty granted to him.

He has cooperated with the investigation and remained available to the Investigating Officer whenever called.
6-aba-2861-2023.doc 6.
The investigation is now complete and the charge-sheet has been filed.
Thus, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary at this stage.
The further presence of the applicant can always be secured at the time of trial.
7. The offences alleged are undoubtedly serious, but seriousness of the offence alone cannot be a ground to deny bail once investigation is complete and the liberty granted has not been misused.

The settled position of law is that the object of bail is to secure the presence of the accused at trial and not to punish him before conviction.
8.
The apprehension expressed by the prosecution regarding the gravity of the offence can be taken care of by imposing suitable conditions.
9. In view of the above, I am of the opinion that the applicant deserves to be granted pre-arrest bail.

10. Hence, following order:

sentences.text: In the event of arrest in connection with Crime Register No. 289 of 2023 registered at Taloja Police Station, for offences under Sections 328, 467, 468, 471, 292, 273, 188 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 26(2) (I), 26, 27, 51 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, the applicant be released on bail on furnishing P.R. bond of Rs.30,000/-, along with one or two sureties in the like amount.
b) The applicant shall remain present before the concerned police station, as and when called by the 6-aba-2861-2023.doc investigating officer.

c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any witness acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer.

d) The applicant shall not obstruct or hamper the police investigation and not to play mischief with the evidence collected or yet to be collected by the police.
e) The applicant shall, at the time of execution of the bond, furnish his address and mobile number to the investigating officer, and the Court concerned, and shall not change the residence till the final disposal of the case.
11. The Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed of accordingly.

(AMIT BORKAR, J.)
